methodological_questions: Can adherence to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predict series winning with only 54 series?
How should adherence be measured from play-by-play and possession records, and how reliable is that measure?
Does the recommended mix predict efficiency at the game level, and does any such link carry over to series winning?
What leakage, confounding, label-error and multiplicity risks affect a test of adherence against winning?

historical_evidence.finding: Holdout games (908 game-team rows, 454 games) where play-type mix was closer to the model's recommended mix showed higher efficiency: raw gap +5.18 ORtg, strength-controlled gap +3.27 ORtg (+0.0193 vs -0.0134 PPP residual). No CI stated. Outcome is team-game efficiency, not series winning.

Playoff adaptation pairs (12 pairs x 74 matchups): 10/12 pairs CONSISTENT and within 0.10 of non-pivot; PNR->PULL_UP and DRIVE->PULL_UP recorded as PIVOT_LOSES; labelled an adequately powered null (B_powered_null).

On-ball defensive scheme labels (DROP/ICE/SWITCH) were populated for 14.9% of DET possessions (10/67) and 3.3% of ORL possessions (2/60); switches_on was not populated by the NBA matchups feed. Verdict: failed_gate.

Inferred defensive scheme change: 61.0% within-game and 67.7% cross-game change, 99% of units changed; transition matrices near-uniform. Caveat: the inferred label cannot separate real adjustment from offensive variation.
Three-level counter ranking (population, team, matchup): L1 and L2 disagree on DRIVE; playoff matchup n ranged 4 to 44.
Play-type PPP across playoff series game buckets (1197 records, no CIs): DRIVE +0.060, CUT +0.114, PNR +0.087, PULL_UP -0.077, POST_UP -0.032; recorded as 'NO CLEAR SIGNAL'.

Observed-vs-recommended mix conformance in single 2025-26 playoff G1s (4 games x 2 offenses): leverage-weighted gap 4.5 to 24.0pp; 4 of 8 sides best matched opener #3, not rank-1; CUT and PNR muted by tagger floor; no outcome comparison.
Team BEST-share consistency across seasons (19 teams with n>=2 seasons); no inferential stability test; BEST share did not identify win% (e.g. IND 4.5% BEST, 71% win; ORL AVOID 59.3%, 0% win).
Superstar sequential suppression (30 stars, min n_after=30): PUTBACK top suppressor for 6+ stars with d up to -0.345; no multiplicity correction; several PUTBACK cells n_after 32 to 95.
Defensive PPP allowed RS vs playoffs (25 teams, min 30 poss per cell): DRIVE -0.268 PPP and share 21.2% to 18.2%; PNR share +12.1pp, flagged as possibly tagging-driven; descriptive only.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labelling on-ball coverage (DROP/ICE/SWITCH) from NBA matchup and play-by-play fields
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as failed_gate: label rates 14.9% (DET) and 3.3% (ORL), small n (5/5 labelled DROP/ICE cells), switches_on unpopulated; failure mechanism A_unanswerable with LABEL_ERROR and small-sample limits.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Inferring defensive scheme change within and across games from labels
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as untestable (A_unanswerable): near-uniform transitions are consistent with label noise, and the label cannot separate defensive adjustment from offensive variation.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Pivoting to a listed counter after suppression to sustain PPP in playoff matchups
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as rejected (B_powered_null): 10/12 pairs near non-pivot; two pairs with enough signal were PIVOT_LOSES; matchup n 5 to 44 with small_sample limitation.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Stable best-counter ranking across population, team and matchup levels
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as inconclusive: L1 and L2 disagree on DRIVE; small_sample and MECHANICAL_FLOOR risk.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using DRIVE PPP trend across series game buckets as an early-series call
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as inconclusive with no clear signal; observational, no CIs, selection and regression-to-the-mean caveat.

evidence_establishes: A team-game-level link between mix alignment with a recommended mix and higher efficiency exists in one holdout (FAM:SF-APPM-001, recorded as supported), with the strength-controlled gap as reported.
Adherence-style and counter-pivot tests at playoff matchup level have been run and returned null or inconclusive results (FAM:SF-APPM-054, FAM:SF-APPM-055, FAM:SF-APPS-010).
Defensive scheme labels from these feeds have been recorded as unreliable at usable rates (FAM:SF-APPS-058, FAM:SF-APPA-005).
evidence_does_not_establish: Any relation between recommended-mix adherence and series winning: no retrieved record tests series outcomes.
Whether the 54-series unit gives usable power for a binary series-winner outcome.
Whether the suppression-conditional recommendation is a valid, pre-specified object: no record states a locked recommendation model.
Causal effect of adherence; retrieved records are observational.
own_inferences: With 54 series, a binary winner outcome offers very few effective observations; detecting even a large effect of adherence on series win would need a near-perfect predictor, which is implausible.
Adherence is a post-treatment behaviour that tracks team quality and in-series adjustment, so naive adherence-win associations are confounded.
Series-level adherence would be built from many game-level mix deviations, inheriting the measurement and label issues recorded for scheme labels and the tagger floor.
The game-level FAM:SF-APPM-001 result is the most transferable piece of evidence, but it does not test the stated question.
uncertainties: The full text of several records was truncated in retrieval (for example SF-APPM-055 and SF-APPA-050); details beyond the visible summaries were not read.
Whether a locked suppression-conditional mix model exists and what its inputs are is not stated in any retrieved record.
Whether FAM:SF-APPM-001 holdout design was pre-registered is not recorded (validation status same_pipeline_validation).
Playoff 2025-26 data is partial before 2026-06-21, so the 2026-06-16 state may miss series outcomes and games.
Whether 54 series is the count for the full analysis window or a subset is not recorded.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieved records show that the closest analogues (mix-conformance, pivot-sustainability, counter ranking, and scheme labelling) were either descriptive, inconclusive, rejected at matchup level, or untestable because of label and sample problems. That pattern, plus the one game-level supported result, moved the decision from proceeding with the series-winning test to not proceeding with it as posed and proposing a reframed game-level test.

blocking_constraints.text: 54 series gives too few independent binary outcomes to detect a plausible adherence effect on series winning.
Defensive scheme and suppression-conditional labels have recorded untestable or unreliable label rates (FAM:SF-APPS-058, FAM:SF-APPA-005).
Adherence is entangled with team strength and in-series adjustment; no retrieved record separates them.

prior_work.summary: Game-level mix alignment and efficiency has one supported holdout result (SF-APPM-001). Pivot and counter-choice questions at matchup level were null or inconclusive (SF-APPM-054, SF-APPM-055). No retrieved record tests series winning or suppression-conditional adherence as a predictor of it.

risks.text: 54 series is too small for a binary winner outcome with multiple adherence and suppression covariates; matchup cells have n 4 to 44 in comparable studies.
Suppression and scheme labels are unreliable (low labelled rates, unpopulated switches_on).
Tagger floors mute CUT and PNR categories (SF-APPS-017), biasing mix measurement.
Team quality and series context drive both adherence and winning; adherence is post-treatment.
Recommended mix and suppression conditioning could use same-series or future possessions if not frozen before the series.
Many play-type by suppressor cells were examined without correction (SF-APPA-050).
Series winning base rate is about 0.5 with favourites dominant, so small adherence effects are hard to separate.
Play-type PPP and defensive schemes shift across seasons and series stages (SF-APPS-010, SF08, SF-APPS-012).
No placebo or negative-control outcome is recorded in any retrieved study.

design.estimand: As posed: effect of game-level adherence to a frozen suppression-conditional recommended mix on series winning. Minimum viable reframed estimand: effect of mix adherence on next-game PPP in playoff holdout games.
design.unit: As posed: series (54). Reframed: team-game, with series as cluster.
design.sample: Reframed: 2022-23 to 2024-25 playoff and regular-season games for training; 2025-26 playoff games (complete from 2026-06-21) as holdout; no series-level test is proposed.
design.power: Compute power before running; with 54 series the series-winning test has very low power. Reframed game-level test should target a pre-specified minimum effect size (for example +0.02 PPP) with cluster-robust intervals.
design.controls: Team strength (pre-series rating), opponent strength, pace, rest, injuries, home court, and lagged PPP; recommended model frozen before the holdout; no in-series information used.
design.falsification: A negative-control outcome (for example adherence vs next-game free-throw rate or possession share unrelated to the mechanism) and a placebo mix from a shuffled recommendation.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register one primary contrast; report all other play-type by suppressor cells as exploratory with Holm correction.
design.decision_rule: Support only if the primary game-level contrast is positive with a cluster-robust 95% CI excluding 0 and the placebo and negative-control contrasts are null; otherwise report as null or uncertain. Do not claim series-winning prediction.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular season and playoffs; 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13; 2025-26 playoffs complete from 2026-06-21 (partial before). Record the snapshot date of each file.

methodological_questions: Can adherence to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predict series winning with only 54 series?
How should adherence be measured from play-by-play and possession records?
What leakage, confounding, and sample-size risks affect a test of recommended-mix adherence against winning?
args.query: defensive suppression counter strategy recommended play mix adherence predicts winning playoff series NBA 2022-23 to 2025-26

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Field guidance:
- historical_evidence and failed_approaches: only records returned by a tool, with the status as recorded; empty lists
  if nothing relevant was returned.
- testability.p_testable: probability that the question can be answered with the stated data at useful statistical power.
- prior_work.already_answered: whether retrieved earlier work already answered substantially the same question.
  Use "unknown" if no earlier work was retrieved. List identifiers you relied on in prior_work.cited.
- predicted_outcome: probabilities (summing to 1) of what a competent test of the question as posed would conclude:
  supported, rejected (adequately powered null), untestable (cannot be tested with this data), artifact (apparent
  effect produced by a flaw), uncertain (inconclusive or inadequately tested).
- decision: proceed, proceed_with_changes (state the changes in design), or do_not_proceed.
- design: a pre-registration-quality plan even if the decision is do_not_proceed (then describe the minimum viable test).
